names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Πατερμούθιος, Κόπρις και Αλέξανδρος οι Οσιομάρτυρες», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. јул ст. ст., „Преп. муч. Патермутије и Коприје“ — „Преп. муч.“ is the rank, „Патермутије и“ is the other name the heading enumerates, and the bare forename is left. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Коприје» — **and this day writes it onto two folders**, this one off entry 3 and `copres-the-egyptian` off entry 4, which the book itself says are different men. So the fold the day makes is between its own two entries, exactly as with the two Procopii on 8 July, and here it is **the source and not the reader** that distinguishes the men. Neither heading offers a by-name to break it with; `copris-of-palestine` and `copris-of-pechenga` hold other forms and are neither of these two.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 1281, «Коприй Египетский, прмч.», with the rank word after the comma left off. STRIPPING THE RANK IS WHAT MAKES THE FOLD: name page 1280 is «Коприй Египетский, иеромонах», the fifth-century presbyter of the Лавсаик and a different man, whose folder is `copres-the-egyptian` and which takes the identical string in this same batch. `fk.mjs` returned no holder before this batch; a two-holder `READ_FOLDS` key is written in the same commit.

death.note: saint.gr dates the martyrdom by the reign and by the campaign: «αποκεφαλίστηκαν με διαταγή του Ιουλιανού του παραβάτη (361 - 363 μ.Χ.), όταν αυτός εκστράτευε κατά των Περσών». No year of birth is given and no year within the reign.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 июля ст. ст. — «Прмчч. Патермуфия , Коприя и мч. Александра (361-363).»

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, second name, and this folder’s man — the disciple of the pair, name page 1281, «Коприй Египетский, прмч.», the one who fell and was restored. The reading life4200 WAS OPENED and is one paragraph: Patermuthius and his disciple Coprius were Egyptian hermits whom the apostate emperor had brought before him and tried to turn to paganism, saying craftily that he too had once served Christ and had learned that only the pagan gods can save; Coprius was taken in by the emperor’s promises and denied Christ, but by his elder’s prayers and tearful admonitions came to know his fall, repented and confessed himself a Christian again; the emperor had him cruelly tortured while Patermuthius strengthened his brother’s courage and patience, and one of the soldiers, by name Alexander, seeing what Coprius suffered, believed in Christ and was sentenced to be burned, while Patermuthius and Coprius were beheaded. THAT IS THE SAME COMPANY, THE SAME REIGN AND THE SAME ORDER OF EVENTS saint.gr gave these three folders, and the line’s «(361-363)» is exactly the interval they already carry. `dates` UNCHANGED. The manner of each death — the sword for two, the fire for Alexander — is in this reading where saint.gr gave only the beheading of all three, and it is recorded here and in no field. The entry names the emperor and no place; «Египетский» on the name pages is the one geography and it is in the stored name forms. No hymn on the day page stands under any of the three names. THE DAY PRINTS TWO ENTRIES, EACH NAMING A PATERMUTHIUS AND A COPRIUS, AND THEY ARE FOUR DIFFERENT MEN WITH FOUR NAME PAGES. The third entry is «Прмчч. Патермуфия , Коприя и мч. Александра (361-363).», the venerable-martyrs under Julian the Apostate, name pages 1744, 1281 and 107; the fourth is «Прпп. Патермуфия и Коприя Египетских (V).», the venerables of the fifth century, name pages 1745 and 1280. Each page lists «День памяти: 9 июля» and no other day, and the two pairs have a reading each, life4200 and life4201, BOTH OPENED. The corpus’s own folders divide the same way: `patermuthius-17-december`, `copris-17-december` and `alexander-17-december` are the martyr trio off saint.gr’s 17 December, and `copres-the-egyptian` is the venerable off doxologia.ro’s and the Охридски пролог’s 9 July. Only the venerable Patermuthius had no folder, and he is the arrival. BECAUSE THE RANK IS WHAT THE CALENDAR USES TO TELL THE PAIRS APART, the stored forms collide once the ranks are stripped, and TWO `READ_FOLDS` KEYS were written in the same commit for the two two-holder folds. TWO ENTRIES OF THIS DAY WERE WITHHELD AND ARE NAMED IN THE REPORT, both folders already carrying a VENERATED russian row on another Julian day: `pancratius-of-tauromenium` on 9 февраля (three hymns on this page left uncopied) and `cyril-of-gortyna` on 6 сентября (two hymns left uncopied). BRIEF-RUSSIAN §4 forbids a draft on such a folder and BRIEF.md §4 sanctions a second-day note; the author has not ruled, so nothing was written for either.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Πατερμούθιος, Κόπρις και Αλέξανδρος οι Οσιομάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The entry enumerates its company — three named men — so it is a folder each, and each relates the other two.** The page's whole narrative is three sentences: Christians full of piety and zeal were tortured and at last beheaded by order of Julian the Transgressor, whose years it gives as 361 to 363, when he was campaigning against the Persians; Copris, a young man, lost his nerve a little at first, but Patermuthius strengthened him with his warm words; and all three underwent the martyr's death chanting hymns to Christ. It names no place at all, so no coordinate is proposed, and it prints no hymn. **The corpus already keeps a `patermuthius-the-martyr` and a `copris-of-palestine`, and neither is one of these: that Patermuthius is the nobleman who suffered on 17 Σεπτεμβρίου with Elias and the bishops Peleus and Nilus under the earlier persecution, and that Copris is a venerable of 24 Σεπτεμβρίου. Two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, and these three are under Julian.** The page carries two epigrams, one in which Copris cries to Patermuthius that he has been made sharer of his life and of his sword, and one which gives Alexander a double crown for ascesis and for the blade; nothing is drafted from them.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.07.2026 (9. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. муч. Патермутије и Коприје“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, the second of the two names its heading enumerates. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **TWO CALENDARS, TWO DAYS**, as on his companion: the Greek row stands on 17 December, this book keeps him on the Julian 9 July, the `serbian` row was `undocumented`, and nothing of the Greek row is touched. **THE SAME STATED YEAR, REFUSED ON THE SAME GROUND, AND THE SENTENCE IS PLURAL.** `death` 361 to 363, display «between 361 and 363», `attested`, off saint.gr’s reading of Julian’s reign and Persian campaign; this book’s 361 lies inside it. „Чесно пострадаше за Христа“ — **they** suffered — is the plural that makes the refusal and the note this folder’s own and not his companion’s, as „пострадаше“ did for the two Roman brothers on 1 July and „Сви пострадаше“ for the Persian company on 6 July. The age of forty-five is an age and not a date. **AND THIS IS THE ONE FOLDER OF THE DAY THAT APOSTATISED AND RETURNED.** The emperor succeeded in turning him from Christ and he cried „Јулијанов сам а не Христов“; rebuked by the elder and warned of the eternal torments he started up and cried before the emperor „Христов сам а не Јулијанов“. Both sentences are written into the life, which is this folder’s whole new content and is the opposite of furniture. `types` UNTOUCHED: `venerable-martyr` is there and „Преп. муч.“ is that word. No `office`, no `locations`. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder already relates `patermuthius-17-december` and `alexander-17-december`, both in both directions. **AND ALEXANDER THE SOLDIER GETS NO ROW, THOUGH HIS FOLDER EXISTS AND RELATES BOTH OF THEM.** „Са њима пострада и Александар, један од царевих војника, који видећи њихову храброст у страдању, и сам поста хришћанин“ — with them suffered also Alexander, one of the emperor’s soldiers, who seeing their courage in suffering became a Christian himself. `alexander-17-december` is a folder, `venerable-martyr`, kept venerated by the Greek calendar on 17 December with the same `death` «between 361 and 363», and **already relates both men in both directions**. He stands in the **body**, and the heading is „Преп. муч. Патермутије и Коприје“: §4 is explicit that a row’s quoted line is the heading, whole, and §5 that the count is what the heading enumerates — **two names**. This is the fifth day running on which a folder the heading does not carry has been refused a row: the six monks on 5 July, Audifax and Abachum on 6 July, the bishop of Tomis on 7 July, the twelve women and the mother on 8 July. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE DAY PRINTS THE SAME TWO NAMES TWICE AND SAYS OUTRIGHT THAT THE MEN ARE DIFFERENT.** Entry 3 is „Преп. муч. Патермутије и Коприје“ and entry 4 is „Преп. Патермутије и Коприје“, and entry 4 opens „Мада истих имена, ови беху различити од оних првих“ — though of the same names, these were different from the first ones. The standing ruling that **two commemorations on one calendar means two men** — which kept the Prologue’s Egyptian monk Дула off `doulas-of-cilicia` on 15 June — is here made by the book itself, in a sentence, and it decides four readings at once. Entry 3’s pair are Преп. муч., venerable-martyrs, beheaded under Julian the Apostate with a soldier Alexander, aged 75 and 45, in 361: that is `patermuthius-17-december` and `copris-17-december`, whose Greek rows stand on 17 December with `death` «between 361 and 363» off Julian’s reign and his Persian campaign, and who relate each other and `alexander-17-december` already. Entry 4’s pair are Преп., venerables and wonderworkers who reposed at the end of the fourth century in deep old age: doxologia keeps **one** of them on this very 9 July as «Sfântul Cuvios Coprie Egipteanul», `venerable`, which is `copres-the-egyptian` — and **entry 4’s Patermuthius has no folder at all**. **ENTRY 4’S PATERMUTHIUS IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE BOOK’S OWN.** He was first the leader of a band of robbers: he had climbed onto the roof of a God-pleasing woman’s house to get in and plunder it, sleep fell on him, and in the sleep he saw **Someone** who threatened him to do evil no more and to repent — so he was not only baptised but tonsured. With his companion he was a great wonderworker, healing every torment and sickness, turning sinners to the right way and prophesying; and a sinner on his deathbed begged him to lengthen his life that he might repent, and after the prayer the saint told him God was adding three years, and the sinner repented and died **exactly three years later**. `ls saints | grep -i patermuth` returns **three** and not one of them is he. `patermuthius-the-martyr` is «Patermuthius the Glorious», a `martyr` whose `death` is 305 to 311 under Maximian Galerius at the hands of Firmilian, kept with Elias on 17 September by three calendars — a martyr of a different persecution fifty years earlier. `patermuthius-17-december` is **entry 3’s man**, whom this very entry exists to tell entry 4’s apart from, so writing entry 4 onto him would be the exact error the Дула ruling forbids. `elias-martyr-with-patermuthius` is the companion of the first. Ruling 3: named here, left out of no life — his story is written into `copres-the-egyptian`’s life, the entry being one entry and the companion’s folder existing — but **no folder from me**, and **no row for any Patermuthius on entry 4**. The three years, the age and the end of the fourth century are written on Copres, whose entry they also are, and nowhere else.
